title: Windows state files inherit the parent directory DACL
description: At commit 5b30b8d6475114bb1312f4bb451f65216d3e7990 the permission helpers are unchanged since 36610e8. The diff 36610e8f012018e3ddd624304dbcf680ae4df56c..5b30b8d6475114bb1312f4bb451f65216d3e7990 does not list src/fsperm.rs, src/store.rs, src/dispatch.rs, or src/agents.rs. The attacker starts as a second local Windows account that can open files under its own token. That account is not the creating user, is not a member of Administrators, and is not SYSTEM or an elevated token. Those two principals are comparable to root, which can already read the Unix 0600 files. The OS principal boundary is that second account's token against the creating user's state files. On Unix, tsk forces the state directory to 0700 and task files such as tsk.json to 0600 so another local user cannot read task data. On Windows, ensure_private_dir, create_private_file, open_lock_file, and tighten_file set no security descriptor and no mode: a missing state directory is created with create_dir_all at fsperm.rs:45, and tsk.json is opened with OpenOptions that apply mode 0600 only under cfg(unix) at fsperm.rs:179. tighten_file is a no-op off Unix at fsperm.rs:302, including on later load at store.rs:756, so this repository never narrows a Windows DACL after creation. src/fsperm.rs is unchanged, and the non-Unix write_launcher body is unchanged. The Windows default is returned at store.rs lines 1439 and 1444, save calls ensure_private_dir at line 829 and tighten_state_files at line 831, and the temp document is created at line 862. The same missing descriptor covers a dispatch launcher. SystemDispatchHost::launcher_file at line 1143 places it at the state directory joined with launchers and a .ps1 name. On non-Unix, write_launcher at line 1834 creates that directory with create_dir_all and writes the script with std::fs::write, not create_private_file. That script base64-embeds profile env values and the task command arguments in powershell_script at agents.rs:650. config.toml temps use the same Unix-only mode at agents.rs:287. The header comment that no permission is claimed off Unix does not show whether the inherited parent DACL already excludes that second account. The installer creates %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\tsk\bin and does not create or ACL the state directory. A second non-admin local account might read %LOCALAPPDATA%\tsk\tsk.json, or a launcher script already stored beside it, if that inherited DACL allows it. Plaintext readable only by the creating account would not cross this boundary. Source cannot show the inherited DACL.
claimed_root_cause: ensure_private_dir, create_private_file, open_lock_file, and tighten_file apply owner-only mode bits only on Unix. On Windows they create the state directory and tsk.json through std::fs with no security descriptor and never call a DACL API, so the directory and tsk.json keep the parent directory's inherited DACL and are not tightened later. SystemDispatchHost::write_launcher on non-Unix is the same gap: it creates the launchers directory with create_dir_all and writes the PowerShell launcher with std::fs::write, not create_private_file, so that file also receives no security descriptor. create_private_temp does the same for config.toml. Source cannot show the inherited DACL.

trace.description: When TSK_STATE_DIR is unset and LOCALAPPDATA is non-empty, the Windows default is that directory joined with tsk. Line 1439 returns PathBuf::from(local).join("tsk"). Lines 1442-1444 fall back to USERPROFILE joined with .tsk when LOCALAPPDATA is empty.
Each supported save calls ensure_private_dir on the state directory at line 829, then tighten_state_files at line 831, before replacing tsk.json.
A missing directory is created with fs::create_dir_all. The Windows-only extra step is reject_reparse_ancestors at lines 35-36. tighten_private_dir, which applies 0700, is cfg(unix) at lines 55-56.

Each existing private state name, including tsk.json, is passed to tighten_file at line 1192. Load at line 756 and save at line 831 both call this function, so a later load is the same no-op off Unix.
The cfg(not(unix)) body at lines 300-303 discards the path. No mode bits and no security descriptor are written.

The temp document is opened with filesystem.create_file. StdFilesystem::create_file at line 325 calls create_private_file. tighten_state_files has already returned at line 831 and does not run again after this create.
OpenOptions is write, create, and truncate at line 175, then open at line 181. mode(0o600) exists only inside cfg(unix) at lines 176-179. The Windows open passes no security descriptor.

Separate from the tsk.json replace, a dispatch launcher is the state directory joined with launchers at line 1146 and the workspace file name. The script therefore lives under the same state directory.

The cfg(not(unix)) body creates the launchers directory with std::fs::create_dir_all and writes the script with std::fs::write. It does not call create_private_file. The Unix body at lines 1825-1831 does. The Windows write passes no security descriptor, and nothing later calls tighten_file on the .ps1.

evidence.description: The module header says Unix state directories are 0700 and files are 0600, and that no permission is claimed on other platforms, where these helpers compile down to plain create and copy.
Before create_dir_all, Windows only calls reject_reparse_ancestors. The directory create attaches no security descriptor.
The directory tighten call is gated by cfg(unix); the Windows function returns after the reparse and directory checks.
options.mode(0o600) is inside the cfg(unix) block that begins at line 176.
open_lock_file sets mode 0600 only inside the cfg(unix) block at lines 244-248. The Windows open passes no security descriptor.
The production AtomicFilesystem create_file implementation is create_private_file, with no Windows security-attribute argument.
Load calls tighten_state_files, which is a no-op off Unix.
After open_lock_file at line 891, tighten_file runs. Off Unix that call does not change a DACL. The same pair is at lines 918-919 and 1123-1125.
Save calls tighten_state_files after ensure_private_dir and before the temp document is created.
The non-empty LOCALAPPDATA branch returns PathBuf::from(local).join("tsk").
When LOCALAPPDATA is unavailable, the Windows fallback returns PathBuf::from(userprofile).join(".tsk").
launcher_file joins the host state directory with launchers. The production write at line 1821 uses that path.
On non-Unix, write_launcher uses std::fs::create_dir_all and std::fs::write. The Unix branch at lines 1825-1831 uses ensure_private_dir and create_private_file.
powershell_script base64-embeds each profile env value, then the command arguments, into the script write_launcher stores.
create_private_temp, used for config.toml, applies mode 0600 only inside cfg(unix) at this line, then opens with no security descriptor on Windows.
The storage guide documents the Windows default as LOCALAPPDATA\tsk, or USERPROFILE\.tsk when LOCALAPPDATA is unavailable, and does not document a Windows ACL.
The Windows installer default directory joins LOCALAPPDATA with Programs\tsk\bin. That is the program directory, not the state directory.
The installer creates that program directory with New-Item. The repository contains no DACL or Set-Acl call.

blockers: The inherited DACL is an operating-system fact. This repository never sets or records a Windows security descriptor. ensure_private_dir, create_private_file, open_lock_file, tighten_file, create_private_temp, and the non-Unix write_launcher path all leave it unset, so source cannot show whether a second non-admin account, which is not the owner and not Administrators or SYSTEM, has an allow ACE on the state directory, tsk.json, or a launcher script.
A Windows DACL observation is required and was not performed. This host is Linux, so it cannot create a Windows profile or query a DACL, and target code was not executed.

validation_plan.local: On a fresh Windows 10 or 11 profile that is not a member of Administrators and is not elevated, leave TSK_STATE_DIR unset and do not pass --state-dir. Run tsk add with a dummy title so the default state directory and tsk.json are created. Do not dispatch and do not create a worktree. As that same user, run icacls with only the path, and no grant, deny, remove, reset, setowner, or inheritance switch, on the new state directory and on tsk.json. Record the DACL. This Linux host cannot run that check.
validation_plan.deployment: On an existing Windows store, run icacls with only the path on the state directory, on tsk.json, and, when present, on the launchers directory and one existing .ps1 under it. Do not change the ACL, do not take ownership, do not dispatch, and do not open the task file or the launcher. Record whether any allow ACE, including an inherited ACE, grants read to a principal other than the owner, SYSTEM, and Administrators.
